screening.reason: Meets inclusion 2/3: analyses all of ABIDE I resting-state fMRI connectivity data for multi-site domain-adaptation ASD identification (diagnostic prediction).

evidence_spans.text: The data used in the current study were provided by ABIDE I ( http://fcon_1000.projects.nitrc.org/indi/abide/), and we use all 1102 subjects (ﬁlter_noglobal) processed by the Conﬁgurable Pipeline for the Analysis of Connectomes (CPAC) [22] for experiments.
evidence_spans.claim: All 1102 ABIDE I subjects (CPAC filter_noglobal preprocessing) were used.

evidence_spans.text:
We conduct experiments on all ABIDE I data (without any data screening), and obtain the mean 73.1%/73.4% accu-
racy on AAL/CC200 atlas
evidence_spans.claim: No data screening/QC exclusion was applied; the full 1102-subject ABIDE I release was used.

evidence_spans.text:
To validate the effectiveness of the proposed LRCDR
method, we conduct inter-site cross-validation experiments on
17 sites from ABIDE database. Speciﬁcally, one site is left
as the target domain for testing, and the remaining 16 sites
as multiple source domains for training.
evidence_spans.claim: Evaluation used leave-one-site-out inter-site cross-validation across all 17 ABIDE I sites.

evidence_spans.text:
The mean time series from 116 regions of interest (ROIs)
based on the automated anatomical labeling (AAL) atlas [23] are used for experiments.
evidence_spans.claim: Functional connectivity features used the AAL atlas (116 ROIs).

evidence_spans.text:
We also use the Craddock 200 (CC200) atlas [31] to
further verify the effectiveness of the LRCDR method and obtain the 73.4% mean accuracy.
evidence_spans.claim: CC200 atlas gave 73.4% mean leave-one-site-out accuracy.

evidence_spans.text:
For inter-site prediction on all ABIDE I data
(1102 subjects from 17 sites), LRCDR obtains the mean
accuracy of 73.1%, superior to the results of the compared
state-of-the-art domain adaptation methods and multi-site
ASD identiﬁcation methods.
evidence_spans.claim: LRCDR achieved 73.1% mean leave-one-site-out accuracy on AAL atlas, outperforming compared domain-adaptation methods.

evidence_spans.text:
In addition, we locate some
meaningful biomarkers: Most of the top important biomark-
ers are inter-network resting-state functional connectivi-
ties (RSFCs).
evidence_spans.claim: Feature-importance analysis identified mostly inter-network RSFCs as the most discriminative connections.

assessments.support: Total N (1102) and the filter_noglobal preprocessing variant are given, but no ASD/TD breakdown is reported in the extractable text, and the authors explicitly state no data screening/QC exclusion was applied: "We conduct experiments on all ABIDE I data (without any data screening)"
Pipeline (CPAC filter_noglobal) and two named atlases (AAL, CC200) with Pearson-correlation connectivity clearly described.
ASD/TD labels are the ABIDE phenotypic diagnosis, independent of the connectivity-derived predictors.

Leave-one-site-out inter-site cross-validation explicitly handles site, but the hyperparameter search over (α, β, γ, λ, η) is not stated to be confined to the training/source domains, leaving open a risk of test-domain leakage: "The parameters (α, β, γ, λ, η) are all searched in the set of {0.001, 0.01, 0.1, 1, 10, 100}."

risk_of_bias.summary: Full ABIDE I release used with no stated QC/exclusion and no ASD/TD breakdown in the extractable text; pipeline and atlases are well described; site is explicitly handled via leave-one-site-out cross-validation, but hyperparameter-search leakage control is not described.

narrative_row.study_design_sample_dataset: Diagnostic prediction; all 1102 ABIDE I subjects from 17 sites, CPAC filter_noglobal preprocessing, no data screening applied, ASD/TD breakdown not in extractable text.
narrative_row.methods: AAL (116 ROIs) and CC200 atlas functional connectivity; Low Rank and Class Discriminative Representation (LRCDR) domain-adaptation method with a linear SVM; leave-one-site-out inter-site cross-validation across all 17 sites.
narrative_row.outcomes: Mean leave-one-site-out accuracy 73.1% (AAL) and 73.4% (CC200), outperforming compared domain-adaptation and multi-site ASD identification methods; top discriminative connections were mostly inter-network RSFCs.
narrative_row.key_limitations: No ASD/TD breakdown or QC/exclusion rule in the extractable text (explicitly no data screening applied); hyperparameter-search leakage control not described; no code or participant list, only supplementary material.
narrative_row.relevance_notes: Demonstrates a domain-adaptation approach explicitly designed to handle ABIDE I site heterogeneity via leave-one-site-out evaluation on the full unscreened release.
